artifacts.summary: Confirms both named lint defects (artifacts/status shape in books-implementation-hard-agent.md; hand-rolled task lookup in both books hard skills), identifies the exact copy-source fix for each from a passing sibling file, traces both to task 297's scaffold commits, and roots the broader completion-gate-passed-anyway question in task 297 Phase 8's Verification-Tier-full phase never actually invoking verify-deploy.sh (and task 326 reproducing the same gap on a second touch of the same files).

memory_candidates.content: lint-agent-contracts.sh Check F (object-shaped artifacts template) and Check E (terminal status presence) can both fail on the SAME file for the SAME reason: a Stage 7 that only references the artifacts/status shape in prose (e.g. "same artifacts shape as the base agent") rather than carrying a literal fenced `"status"`/`"artifacts"` JSON block. Fixing by copying the passing sibling's exact fenced block resolves both checks in one edit, since the template itself carries both a `"status": "implemented"` line and the object-shaped `artifacts` array.

A plan phase declaring `**Verification Tier**: full` is not mechanically tied to an actual verify-deploy.sh invocation anywhere in the authoring or execution path -- it is a documentation convention only. Two real plans (task 297's scaffold Phase 8, and the entirety of task 326) declared/implied full-tier completion while never naming verify-deploy.sh in their own task list, each substituting a self-chosen validator subset instead; nothing in validate-artifact.sh or any lint catches the mismatch between a declared `full` tier and the actual commands a phase's checklist runs. plan-format.md's own text defines `full` as "the complete gate set for the repository" but never names the concrete command (`bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh`) that satisfies it -- every other located full-tier precedent (tasks 165, 127, 184, 265, 250) independently converged on naming it explicitly.
